summary: Four Brothers lookout in Del Norte County: a tower around 1922, a portable trailer from the 1960s or 1973, and a two-story cab built in 2008 that the FFLA lists as standing.

facts.design: Two-story cab built in 2008; the earlier timber tower used a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Six Rivers National Forest

events.note: A guard was working from a station on Ship Mt. in July 1914 (Siskiyou Bulletin, quoted by Forest Lookouts); the Register says a lookout may have been there as early as 1914
Timber tower with a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab erected circa 1922 (Register); a standard cabin was packed 26 miles in (1939 forest history, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Al Gastman took over the lookout station in August 1922 (Blue Lake Advocate, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
During a lightning storm one lookout reported lightning strikes in 2648 places in his territory
AWS Station 'Mike 8-1' (Aircraft Warning Service) placed on inactive status, October 17, 1943
Portable trailer lookout in use at the site since 1973 (FFLA 2008 report); the Register dates the trailer replacement to the 1960s
Portable lookout trailer removed and the road to the top of the mountain improved
New two-story lookout station built, replacing the portable trailer
Registered October 17, 2019 as US 1313, CA 136; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.proposed: 1922 built (timber tower with Region 5 Plan 4AR cab); lookout use possibly from 1914
corrections.why: The Register says a lookout 'may have been' on the peak as early as 1914 and dates the timber tower to circa 1922. A 1914 build date is not supported.

corrections.current: 2007 assessed (Surveyed to see whether it could be moved from California to Oregon for restoration; waiting on transfer of ownership.)
corrections.proposed: 2007 removed: portable trailer removed and road to the top improved
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts history's 2007 entry reports trailer removal and road work. No page read mentions a survey for a move to Oregon or an ownership transfer, so that claim is unsupported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register puts the portable trailer in the 1960s. The FFLA 2008 report says it had been used at the site since 1973. The record uses 1973 with the Register's 1960s noted in the event.

The Register calls the site Four Brothers #3, and a 1941 survey described a station on peak 3. A later note places the current house on Peak #4, the southernmost of the four. The story follows the Register's name and notes the disagreement.

The Register's coordinates (41.735609, -123.792981) match the FFLA entry 'Ship Mountain (old)', which is marked Gone. The FFLA standing entry sits at 41.72813, -123.79548, which the record uses. The two points are roughly a kilometre apart; the record keeps the standing entry's point.

notes_for_editor: Current access and visitor status were not found in any source read, so no access level is given. The 2008 FFLA report's trailer date (1973) and the Register's 1960s date are both kept. The 'moved to Oregon' claim in the record's 2007 event is not in any page read and is proposed for removal. The Register's photos (credited to Ron Kemnow and Fred Johnson) have no URLs captured, so no photos are added. The 1914 staffing entry relies on a single 1914 newspaper item as quoted by Forest Lookouts, not on the newspaper itself.
